subject: Agriculture
title: One-Third Wasted
description: A short lesson to help you apply One-Third Wasted.

hook.text: Every year, 1.3 billion tons of food is lost or wasted globally. That's one-third of everything produced.

buildup.text: In developing countries, food is lost after harvest—poor storage, no refrigeration, bad roads.

discovery.text: In rich countries, food is wasted at retail and consumer levels—thrown out for imperfect looks or passed sell-by dates.

twist.text: If food waste were a country, it would be the third largest emitter of greenhouse gases—after China and the US.

climax.text: The land, water, and energy used to produce wasted food equals throwing away 25% of all agricultural resources.

punchline.text: We grow enough for 10 billion. We throw away enough for 2 billion.

quiz.question: If food waste were a country, where would it rank in greenhouse gas emissions?

details.summary: Roughly one-third of all food produced globally is lost or wasted each year—about 1.3 billion tons. This topic quantifies the scale of food loss and waste, identifies where it occurs along the supply chain, and summarizes strategies for cutting it.
details.whyItMatters: Wasted food represents wasted land, water, energy, and labor. Halving food waste by 2030 is a UN Sustainable Development Goal because it would free resources to feed hundreds of millions more people.
takeaways: About 1.3 billion tons of food—one-third of production—is lost or wasted annually
In developing countries loss occurs mainly at harvest and storage; in rich countries at retail and consumer level
Cutting food waste in half would reduce agricultural greenhouse gas emissions by 6–8%

faq.question: Where does most food waste occur in the supply chain?
faq.answer: In developing countries, most loss happens post-harvest due to poor storage, transport, and processing. In developed countries, most waste occurs at retail and consumer stages due to cosmetic standards, overstocking, and household disposal.

faq.question: What would halving global food waste achieve?
faq.answer: Halving food waste would save enough food to feed over a billion additional people, free up millions of hectares of farmland, conserve vast amounts of freshwater, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by hundreds of millions of tons annually.
